days.title: East Shore Landmarks and Engineering
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Staumauer
stops.detail: At the center is the 48 m high and heritage-listed dam wall with its two historic gate towers and the two power plant buildings at the foot of the wall.

stops.name: Hemfurth-Edersee
stops.detail: Over a straight line of twelve kilometers, the reservoir winds through the Eder Valley from its confluence before the village of Herzhausen (near Vöhl) in the west to the dam wall near Hemfurth-Edersee in the east.

stops.name: Schloss Waldeck
stops.detail: Overlooked by Waldeck Castle, the dam, also known simply as Edersee, forms a large-scale leisure and recreation area together with the Kellerwald-Edersee National Park and the Kellerwald-Edersee Nature Park.

days.title: Nature Reserves and the Southern Shore
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Nationalpark Kellerwald-Edersee
stops.detail: In the south, the reservoir borders the Eder Heights, a mountain region in the north of the Kellerwald, which together with the northern slopes of the Eder trough form the Kellerwald-Edersee National Park.

stops.name: Bringhausen
stops.detail: The villages of Asel and Bringhausen, which were located in the Eder valley, were rebuilt at higher elevations above the emerging Lake Edersee after they had been demolished or dismantled, but Berich, which was also affected, was rebuilt around 21 km from its former location on the territory of the town of Bad Arolsen.
